record.paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
record.context_brief: Perfect matchings in non-bipartite regular multigraphs
record.original_question: Let omega(n,n,r) be the minimum number of perfect matchings among r-colorable r-regular multigraphs on 2n vertices, in the notation of the source. For each fixed r >= 3, does omega(n,n,r) grow exponentially as n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.1. ω(n, n, r) has an exponential growth in n for a fixed r ≥ 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $n\ge 1$ and $r\ge 3$, consider the class $\mathcal{G}(n,r)$ of $r$-regular multigraphs on $2n$ vertices that are $r$-edge-colorable, i.e., whose edge sets can be partitioned into $r$ perfect matchings (equivalently, $r$-regular multigraphs of chromatic index $r$). For $G\in\mathcal{G}(n,r)$, let $m(G)$ denote the number of perfect matchings of $G$, and define
$$\omega(n,n,r)\;=\;\min_{G\in\mathcal{G}(n,r)} m(G).$$
Question: For each fixed integer $r\ge 3$, does $\omega(n,n,r)$ grow exponentially in $n$? That is, do there exist constants $c=c(r)>1$ and $K=K(r)>0$ such that $\omega(n,n,r)\ge K\,c^n$ for all sufficiently large $n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The cubic case ($r=3$) follows from the Lovász–Plummer conjecture, proved by Esperet, Kardoš, King, Kráľ and Norine (2011), which establishes exponentially many perfect matchings in every bridgeless cubic graph (in particular every 3-edge-colorable cubic graph). For general fixed $r\ge 4$, the analogous exponential lower bound for the minimum number of perfect matchings among $r$-edge-colorable $r$-regular multigraphs does not appear to be settled in the literature; Schrijver's theorem gives the bipartite analogue, but the non-bipartite case for $r\ge 4$ remains open as far as available sources indicate.

status_evidence.title: Exponentially many perfect matchings in cubic graphs (Esperet, Kardoš, King, Kráľ, Norine)
status_evidence.snippet: The Lovász–Plummer conjecture that every bridgeless cubic graph has exponentially many perfect matchings was proved in 2011.
status_evidence.claim: The case r=3 of the exponential growth question is resolved affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Pairwise Disjoint Perfect Matchings in r-Edge-Connected r-Regular Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses class 1 r-graphs (those whose edges partition into r perfect matchings) and related conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: The class of r-edge-colorable r-regular multigraphs is studied, but exponential lower bounds on the number of perfect matchings for r>=4 are not established there.
